```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A names a payer (engineering leads or CTOs buying through a team budget) and a billing path (GitHub App or Marketplace subscription). Idea B says outright that it has no defined payer and no evidence of an institutional buyer.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence comes from three independent threads describing production incidents with business cost, such as user complaints and '40% of our customers depended on it'. That pain sits closer to a budget line than Idea B's personal-comfort testimonials.",
    "Idea A has a published paid price point from a direct competitor (apidrift.co at $29/mo flat), which suggests some willingness to pay in a B2B setting. Idea B's pricing anchor is Yoodli, a broader and enterprise-certified product. B's closest niche competitors mostly have unlisted, free, or quote-based pricing, and Convo's price is only inferred from a user review.",
    "Idea A's main channels (GitHub Marketplace, community posts) cost little cash and match how a solo operator would distribute. Idea B's brief cites $20–50 per user for ASO and agency fees of $10k–18k/month, which are hard to recoup at $8–20/month.",
    "Idea B carries extra risk that Idea A does not: health-claim and privacy obligations around recorded voice and possible minors, plus open professional skepticism (r/slp) about the efficacy of pragmatics interventions for autistic users.",
    "Idea A has serious weaknesses of its own: six direct competitors, three of them free, a documented roughly 8x false-positive problem in raw spec diffing, and trust friction over PR access to source code. Even so, it reaches a paying customer through a more evidenced path than Idea B."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's strongest outcome testimonial ('I used to freeze up before every phone call... I just do it now') is an App Store review hand-picked for a competitor's (Convo's) own marketing page. It is curated and not independent. It shows a competitor's success story, not demand for a new entrant, and it says nothing about willingness to pay. This matters most because Idea B has no defined payer at all.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both briefs describe crowded categories with free incumbents, and neither shows a converted paying customer for a new entrant. Idea A wins mainly because it has a defined B2B payer, a priced comparable, and incident-driven demand, while Idea B has an undefined payer and costly acquisition. Some of Idea A's channel evidence is weak: the $248 median CAC comes from a page flagged for a prompt-injection attempt and is treated as directional only. Idea A's case would also weaken if the free competitors keep its conversion rates near zero."
}
```
